title: Threes in the Table
statement: A multiplication table has $10$ rows and $10$ columns, both numbered from $1$ to $10$, and the entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is $i \cdot j$. Equal products in different places are separate entries: for example, $12$ appears four times, as $2 \cdot 6$, $3 \cdot 4$, $4 \cdot 3$ and $6 \cdot 2$. What is the sum of all the entries in the table that are multiples of $3$?
hints: Find the sum of all $100$ entries, and separately the sum of the entries that are not multiples of $3$.
Row $i$ adds up to $i \cdot (1 + 2 + \dots + 10)$, so the whole table adds up to $(1 + 2 + \dots + 10)^2$. Since $3$ is prime, a product $i \cdot j$ is a multiple of $3$ exactly when $i$ or $j$ is.

So the entries that are not multiples of $3$ are the products $i \cdot j$ with neither $i$ nor $j$ a multiple of $3$. They form a smaller multiplication table on the numbers $1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10$, and its sum factorises in the same way.
solution: Row $i$ adds up to $55i$, so the whole table adds up to $55 \cdot (1 + 2 + \dots + 10) = 55^2$. As $3$ is prime, $i \cdot j$ is not a multiple of $3$ exactly when neither $i$ nor $j$ is. The numbers from $1$ to $10$ that are not multiples of $3$ add up to $55 - 3 - 6 - 9 = 37$, so in the same way the entries that are not multiples of $3$ add up to $37^2$. The answer is $55^2 - 37^2 = 18 \cdot 92 = 1656$.
